messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: Metropolis Algorithm
parts:
[back on stan-dev]

The next step would be to make Metropolis callable
from stan/gm/command so that there was a command-line
option to run Metropolis.

So it'd be something like:

./executable_model --metrop --epsilon-metrop=0.1

if you wanted to start with a simple independent
normal(0,epsilon) jumping rule.

Once that's working, the next step will be to
do diagonal adaptation, so each parameter has
a jumping distance estimated from the data during warmup.
That needs to be merged in the same way as the adaptive
HMC and NUTS implementations.

Then, a full covariance matrix estimate along the lines
of what Yuanjun did for HMC.

Then we'll have a pretty state of the art Metropolis-Hastings
implementation as part of Stan.

One motivation for this project is to evaluate Metropolis
vs. HMC and NUTS. Another is to give you (Peter) some
experience writing samplers so that you can take on harder
problems in the future. You should probably read the MC
and MCMC chapters of the Stan manual if you haven't already,
just to get an idea of how this all gets used downstream.

- Bob

>> The control is from the outside. This uses
>> what's called an Iterator in the world
>> of programming patterns (sort of like algorithms,
>> only more vague).
>>
>> An outside program calls next_impl to retrieve
>> samples. We can use the same control for number
>> of loops as we use for our other commands.
>>
>> So the usage from the outside is like this:
>>
>> metropolis<RNG> m(...);
>> for (int i = 0; i < MAX_ITERATIONS; ++i) {
>> sample = m.next();
>> ... do something with sample ...
>> }
>>
>> If you look at stan/gm/command.hpp, you'll see where
>> the other samplers get called like this.
>>
>> - Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Metropolis Algorithm
parts:
I'm refactoring all of that code right now, but if you throw it into something like next_impl it won't to too hard to update. In particular, you'd want to mirror the variance/covariance estimation of the NUTS algorithms which do something like

void var_adapter::_learn_variance(Eigen::VectorXd& var, ps_point& z) {

++_adapt_var_counter;

std::vector<double>& q = z.q;
Eigen::Map<Eigen::VectorXd> x(&q[0], q.size());

++_sum_n;
_sum_x += x;
_sum_x2 += x.cwiseAbs2();

if (_adapt_var_counter == _adapt_var_next) {

_adapt_var_next *= 2;

_sum_x /= _sum_n;
_sum_x2 /= _sum_n;

var = _sum_x2 - _sum_x.cwiseAbs2();

const double norm = var.squaredNorm() / static_cast<double>(var.size());

if (norm) {
var /= norm;
}
else
var.setOnes();

_sum_n = 0;
_sum_x.setZero();
_sum_x2.setZero();

}

}

I can't figure out where this would go. Currently, I have this in metropolis_rw:

#ifndef __STAN__MCMC__METROPOLIS_RW__
#define __STAN__MCMC__METROPOLIS_RW__

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

#include <stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/normal.hpp>
#include <stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/uniform.hpp>
#include <boost/random/mersenne_twister.hpp>

namespace stan {
  namespace mcmc {

    template <class BaseRNG = boost::mt19937>
    class metropolis : public adaptive_sampler {
    private:

      std::vector<double> params_r;
      std::vector<int> params_i;
      double log_prob;
      stan::model::prob_grad *_model;
      BaseRNG base_rng;
      double epsilon;

    public:
    metropolis(stan::model::prob_grad& model,
      const std::vector<double>& par_r,
      const std::vector<int>& par_i,
      bool adapt,
      double eps = 1,
      std::ostream* error_msgs = 0,
      std::ostream* output_msgs = 0)
      : adaptive_sampler(adapt, error_msgs, output_msgs),
params_r(par_r.size()), params_i(par_i.size()), _model(&model), base_rng(BaseRNG(std::time(0))), epsilon(eps) {
      set_params(par_r, par_i);
    }

      /**
       * Destructor.
       *
       * The implementation for this class is a no-op.
       */
      ~metropolis() { }
  
      void set_params( const std::vector<double>& par_r,
      const std::vector<int>& par_i) {
if(par_r.size() != params_r.size())
 throw std::invalid_argument("metropolis::set_params double params must match in size");
if(par_i.size() != params_i.size())
 throw std::invalid_argument("metropolis::set_params int params must match in size");
params_r = par_r;
params_i = par_i;

log_prob = _model->log_prob(params_r, params_i, _error_msgs);
      }

      void write_adaptation_params(std::ostream& /*o*/) {
      }

      /**
       * Return the next sample.
       *
       * @return The next sample.
       */
      sample next_impl() {
      
      std::vector<double> new_params_r(params_r.size());

      for(size_t i = 0; i < new_params_r.size(); i++)
new_params_r[i] = stan::prob::normal_rng(params_r[i], epsilon, base_rng);

      if (!this->adapting()) { 
epsilon = this->mean_stat();
      }

      double new_log_prob = _model->log_prob(new_params_r, params_i, _error_msgs);

      double adapt_stat = std::min(std::exp(new_log_prob - log_prob), 1.0);

      double u = stan::prob::uniform_rng(0,1,base_rng);
   
      if(u < adapt_stat)
{
 params_r = new_params_r;
 log_prob = new_log_prob;  
}

        double avg_eta = 1.0 / this->n_steps();
        this->update_mean_stat(avg_eta,adapt_stat);

return mcmc::sample (params_r, params_i, log_prob);
    }
    };
  }
}
#endif


I would imagine that we would want something like update_mean_stat for each param_r and then use the mean_stat for each param_r from the burn in to determine the epsilon for the actual sampling. However, I'm not sure where this would go or be stored. I've tried looking at the HMC and Nuts samplers but can't seem to figure it out.


Thanks,
Peter
